title: Herod was troubled (Matthew 2:1–12)
hook: the wise men rejoice; the king, and all Jerusalem with him, are afraid
tomorrow: why is a woman from Genesis crying in Matthew?

segments.voice: Yesterday a man woke from a dream and did it without a word: Emmanuel, God with us. Now the child is born, and the news gets out.
screen: `GOD WITH US.` → `NOW THE NEWS GETS OUT.`

segments.voice: A phone lights up with good news: the job, the yes, the baby on the way. Somewhere, someone else reads the same news and goes cold. Matthew's second chapter opens on a day like that. Strangers from the east walk into Jerusalem and ask, out loud: "Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him." They ask it a short walk from the palace of the man who already has that job.
screen: `SAME NEWS, TWO FACES.` → `STRANGERS FROM THE EAST.` → `WHERE IS HE THAT IS BORN KING?`

segments.voice: Matthew answers with two reactions, side by side. The palace first: "When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him." A king with soldiers and walls, shaken by a newborn. He gathers the chief priests and scribes, who point him to Bethlehem, and he sends the strangers on, asking them to bring word back so he can come and worship too. Then the road: "When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy." Same news. One side shaking, the other overjoyed. In a house they find the child with Mary his mother, bow down, and open their treasures: "gold, and frankincense, and myrrh." One to tell a friend tonight: Matthew counts the gifts, never the visitors. Three wise men is a later tradition. Then the quiet ending: "being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way." No showdown with the king. They simply don't take the old road home. Some readers hear a clever escape. Others hear more: people who have met the child don't go back the way they came. Same star, same city. What differs is what each one has to lose.
screen: `THE PALACE: HEROD WAS TROUBLED.` · `THE ROAD: EXCEEDING GREAT JOY.` · `GOLD, FRANKINCENSE AND MYRRH.` · `WARNED IN A DREAM.` · then, large: `THEY WENT HOME ANOTHER WAY.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let one piece of good news come up, yours or someone else's: a change, a new person, a call to something bigger. Notice whether any part of you tightened when it arrived. Don't scold that part; ask it quietly what it's guarding, and let the breath keep coming.
Herod was troubled. A king, and a whole city with him, shaken by news of a child, while strangers under a star rejoice.
Your line: they went home another way. One meeting changed the road back. Go gently.

fork.setup: a friend comes home from a summer away, kinder and calmer. at her first family dinner back, the old argument with her brother starts up. what would going home another way look like?
options: skip the fight she always joins, without announcing why.
give a speech about how much she's changed this summer.
act exactly as before, so nobody feels awkward.
fork.reveal: the wise men didn't confront Herod or announce anything. warned in a dream, they simply took a different road home.

original.note: Greek: magi, the word behind Matthew's wise men from the east.

trapdoor: what you thought: Herod was a little worried.
what it means: the king, and all Jerusalem with him, shaken by news of a newborn king.
what a scholar hears: Matthew pairs two reactions to one piece of news: troubled in the palace, exceeding great joy under the star. strangers from the east worship while the capital trembles.
guess: a king shaken by news of a newborn rival
a king sick in bed with a long fever
a king at war with a city in the east
recall: a family line, traced name by name

chat.says: asked dad if Uncle Dale can come to Pop's party. he went real quiet. why is good news scary?
options: One star scared Herod and thrilled the wise men. Good news can threaten what someone guards. Give him time.
Quiet means no. When Herod went quiet, it was over, so drop the party idea for now.
Good news only scares people hiding something, like Herod. Your dad must be hiding something.
chat.meaning: In Matthew one piece of news troubled a king and brought strangers exceeding great joy. Fear is often guarding something; it isn't always a no.

Herod.meaning: the king in Jerusalem in Matthew's story of Jesus' birth

Bethlehem.meaning: the town where Matthew says Jesus was born

frankincense.meaning: a fragrant resin burned as incense

scribes.meaning: teachers and copyists of the law

notes: Myth: Matthew never gives the number of wise men; three gifts are named (2:11). The number three is a later tradition and is not stated here.
Herod's request that they bring word 'that I may come and worship him also' (2:8) is paraphrased.
'In a house' follows 2:11 ('when they were come into the house'). Confirm.
Two readings of 'another way' (a clever escape; people changed by meeting the child) are given as 'some readers / others', without ranking.
howItsDone: Epiphany and the nativity-figures custom is hedged as 'some homes and churches'.
